planting.note: Grow mounted on cork bark, driftwood, or wire in bright indirect to gentle direct morning light; needs no soil whatsoever. Water by dunking or misting, then shake off excess water and allow to dry within a few hours to prevent rot.

directions: Grow in bright indirect to gentle direct morning sun. Tillandsia fuchsii is a small Mexican species with unusually fine, hair-thin, densely clustered silvery leaves that give the whole plant a soft, feathery, almost fuzzy texture unlike the stiffer, broader leaves of many other air plants. It readily forms dense clumps of many small heads over time, each eventually producing tiny tubular purple flowers from among the finely divided foliage. Like all tillandsias it has no functional roots and absorbs water and nutrients through specialized leaf scales; dunk or mist regularly, then shake off excess water and let the plant dry within a few hours, since standing water at the base causes rot.

planting.note: Grow mounted on cork bark, driftwood, or wire in bright indirect to gentle direct morning light; needs no soil whatsoever. Bergeri is among the more cold-tolerant tillandsia species and clumps vigorously.

directions: Grow in bright indirect to gentle direct morning sun. Tillandsia bergeri is an Argentine species with narrow, silvery, recurving leaves forming a compact rosette that offsets prolifically, quickly building into a dense, ball-like clump of many heads that can be mounted as a single dramatic specimen. Bright violet-blue tubular flowers emerge from a pink-bracted spike, providing good seasonal color contrast against the silvery foliage. It tolerates cooler temperatures somewhat better than many air plant species, making it a good choice for a covered porch in zone 8-9. Water by dunking or misting, then shake off excess water and allow to dry within a few hours, since standing water at the base causes rot.

planting.note: Grow mounted on cork bark or driftwood in bright indirect to gentle direct morning light; needs no soil whatsoever. Funckiana's trailing, branching habit suits a hanging mount better than an upright display.

directions: Grow in bright, direct to lightly filtered sun for best flowering and compact growth. Tillandsia funckiana has slender, curling, succulent leaves along thin, branching, trailing stems, quite different from the tight, symmetrical rosettes of most tillandsia species, and produces vivid, tubular, bright orange-red flowers directly from the leaf axils rather than a separate central spike, giving an especially showy, prolonged bloom. Its branching habit allows a single plant to develop into a multi-stemmed cluster over time, well suited to a hanging mount where the trailing growth can be appreciated. Water by dunking or misting, then shake off excess water and allow to dry within a few hours, since standing water causes rot.

planting.note: Grow mounted on cork bark, driftwood, or wire in bright indirect to gentle direct morning light; needs no soil whatsoever. Capitata is one of the larger commonly grown tillandsia species.

directions: Grow in bright indirect to gentle direct morning sun. Tillandsia capitata forms a substantial, broad rosette of stiff, silvery-green leaves that flush a rosy blush toward the center as the plant approaches bloom, when a colorful bracted flower spike with violet-blue tubular flowers emerges, providing a dramatic, long-lasting color display well before and after the individual flowers open. Its larger scale compared to miniature species like Tillandsia ionantha makes it a strong single specimen for mounting rather than a component of a mixed cluster. Water by dunking or misting, then shake off excess water and allow to dry completely within a few hours, since standing water at the base causes rot.

common_name: Brachycaulos Air Plant (Blushing Red Rosette Tillandsia)

planting.note: Grow mounted on cork bark, driftwood, or wire in bright indirect to gentle direct morning light; needs no soil whatsoever. Brachycaulos flushes its brightest red with strong light just before blooming.

directions: Grow in bright indirect to gentle direct morning sun for the strongest blush color. Tillandsia brachycaulos forms a soft, spreading rosette of thin, pliable, green leaves that flush a vivid, near-total red across the entire plant as it approaches bloom, one of the most dramatic whole-plant color changes among commonly grown tillandsia species, rivaling the blush of the smaller Tillandsia ionantha but on a larger scale. Small violet tubular flowers emerge from the center once the red coloring peaks. After flowering, the parent produces offsets that can be left in place to form a clustering clump or separated once well rooted. Water by dunking or misting, then shake off excess water and allow to dry within a few hours to prevent rot.
